verdicts.why: Replenishment named plainly; the word takes no side on what is refilled.
Reclaiming wasteland is described, not praised or scorned, by this word.
Likeness in appearance is a plain observation; a resemblance can be welcome or not without the word shifting.
Undertaking a journey is stated without any attitude toward the traveller.
Changing location is bare motion; nothing about the mover is judged.
A pleasure trip is named neutrally; the pleasure is the referent, not the speaker's approval.
Being carried in a vehicle is plain description.
Crossing a road or region is described without judgement.
Itinerant movement for work or preaching is named, not sneered at or admired.
Applies equally to unexpected happiness and unexpected trouble; the word reports surprise, not approval or dismay.
Gaining something with effort is the meaning; any credit implied belongs to the deed, not to the word's attitude.
Putting something into effect is a plain statement of completion.
In the 'accomplished fact' sense the word says only that a thing is done, not that it was good to do; the packet's sentences are the other, skilled-lady sense.
Settled and unconditional is a state, and this word takes no side on whether it should have been settled.
'Alive to the disgrace' means keenly aware of it; the keenness is meaning, and the word neither praises nor mocks the aware person.
Possessing life is a bare fact about the referent.
In operation is a status report with no attitude attached.
A volcano capable of erupting is described technically.
Something that promotes well-being is a good referent named in a plain word; the word itself does not add approval.
Financial assistance is named by its neutral official term; any stigma belongs to attitudes toward the referent, not to the word.
A charity performance is a category label, not a judgement of it.
Being extant is the barest of predicates; the sentences apply it to wickedness and fortune alike.
Chosen over 'live' for how someone gets by, it diminishes the life to bare, joyless survival ('merely exist on that wage'), and a learner should know it sounds bleak.
Causing fear is named without any stance on the frightener or the frightened; differences from scare or terrify are degree and register, not attitude.
It praises: choosing it over 'ethical' or 'principled' expresses esteem and admiration for the person's integrity, which is why it is so readily used ironically.
